$description: DHCW Single Record Design System — Border tokens. Covers border colours (including the fourth 'subtle' variant), border widths, and corner radii. Three-tier model: Global (Primitives) → Semantic (Single Record). Sync source: Figma variable collections.

border.$description: Semantic border colour tokens. Alias tier — lives in the Single Record Figma variable collection with Light and Dark mode values.

subtle.$description: Ultra-light border for row dividers and internal table separators. Use only on white or near-white backgrounds where Border/Default would be too prominent. Do not use as the only structural indicator on a surface.

default.$description: Standard border for inputs, cards, and section dividers.

strong.$description: High-contrast border for section edges, active table rows, and structural dividers that must be clearly visible.

focus.$description: Focus ring colour — Cyan/700 (DDR-006). Applied to all interactive elements on keyboard focus. Always paired with Border/Width/Strong (2px) and an inner gap ring.

width.$description: Border width tokens. Integer pixel values only — no sub-pixel widths. Global values in Primitives; semantic aliases in Single Record.

default.$description: Standard 1px border for inputs, cards, dividers, and section edges.

strong.$description: Emphasis border for active states, selected rows, and focus ring outer stroke.

radius.$description: Corner radius tokens. Conservative scale suited to clinical and administrative UI. Prefer flatter radii for data-dense contexts; reserve Radius/LG and Radius/Full for overlay and decorative elements.

none.$description: No rounding. Use for tables, data grids, full-bleed containers, elements that must butt against screen edges or adjacent cells.

sm.$description: Subtle rounding. Use for form inputs, text areas, select controls, inline tags, small badges, and chips.

md.$description: Standard rounding. Use for buttons, cards, panels, notification banners, and tooltips. Default for most interactive components.

lg.$description: Prominent rounding. Use for modals, side drawers, floating menus, and large overlay surfaces.

full.$description: Pill shape. Use for status chips, avatar rings, toggle switches, and search input end-caps. Not appropriate for rectangular content containers.
